newsitem.title: UK: UK CONSERVATIVES BLAME INFLATION RISE ON BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: UK CONSERVATIVES BLAME INFLATION RISE ON BUDGET.

text.p: Britain's opposition Conservatives on Tuesday blamed the rise in inflation in July on Chancellor Gordon Brown's budget measures early in the month.

Industry spokesman Michael Fallon said official data showing the underlying rate of consumer price inflation at 3.0 percent against 2.7 percent in June were "further official confirmation that his (Brown's) anti-inflation credentials are wearing thin". "Labour's decision to jack up taxes -- starting with a higher-than-expected rise in petrol duty -- has fed straight through into higher prices," Fallon said.
He said Brown must now tell local authorities and the National Health Service whether they would be compensated for the higher-than-expected rise in prices.
"No wonder the Bank of England raised interest rates (by 1/4 point) last week. They knew that Gordon Brown had injected extra inflationary pressure into the system," Fallon said.
